reviews.review: Very good! Waiting for more updates :D

Solid early access game with constant updates, pretty difficult game but feels very rewarding. Dungeon runs like that of Binding of Isaac or Hammerwatch, only 3 heroes (classes) right now. Some weapon combos in the game are 110% overpowered and pretty much the only thing I use for a run, so I hope to see some more balancing between all weapons.

[h1] Gunfire Reborn [/h1]

[b] Gunfire Reborn  [/b] is another title to the ever expanding list of early access roguelites, but it changes enough to be given a shot. It has its own unique charms and features while staying true to the genre, and at an $11.99 price point is honestly a steal!

[h1] Story & Characters [/h1]

[b] Narrative [/b] 
Like most roguelites, the story is more of an afterthought in Gunfire Reborn. While it may not have exciting narratives with fancy character development, it does provide a unique premise with a setting that is often underutilized. The setting is heavily inspired by ancient chinese lore, which provides a sense of mystery and sacredness to all aspects of the game. With typical things you would associate with that setting, such as pandas, tombs, kegs, monks, etc. While it may not be the most unique setting for games as a whole, it is refreshing to experience it with a different light in the roguelite genre.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2122007020
[h3] Story & Characters rating: 7.5/10 [/h3]

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

[b] Combat [/b]
Now we get to the fun part, the gunplay in Gunfire Reborn is top notch for an FPS roguelite. Combat in this game revolves around balancing your movement around the stage with the help of your dash ability, all while firing your three weapon slots, throwing grenades, and using your abilities. It is certainly not a shooter where you are meant to take your time with calculated shots, and more in the run around like sonic with a bazooka realm of gunplay. It really is a fast paced shooter that constantly ramps up the difficulty until you reach your limit.

[b] Loot [/b]
With 39 weapons to choose from, ranging from a default pistol to fire breathing lizards and poison tipped kunai blades there is something for everyone. You get your default pistol permanently, and can pick from any weapon for your last two slots. And then add on 100 different occult scrolls, that can drastically change your build, while also upgrading your characters abilities there is a lot of variety in potential builds. If there is to be one department Gunfire Reborn delivers it has to be the sheer amount of tools at your disposal.

[b] Progression [/b]
A common trend in most roguelites now-a-days is to add a form of progression outside of actually being in a run, and it’s present in Gunfire Reborn. During your run you get a form of currency called soul essence, which is earned at a very slow rate. Then in return you can use these soul essences to upgrade different aspects of your character from health, shields, ammo count, drop modifiers, and much more. This adds a whole new level to the game, as instead of taking it one run at a time it turns into gearing and leveling your character for complete destruction. I will warn you that at the end of a run all your currency earned must be spent to upgrade right away, so if you get 35 soul essence and your health upgrade costs 30 that extra 5 will be lost as it's unable to be spent. This encourages a slow evolution of power until you eventually become an unstoppable force. And each different character has a separate talent tree, so be prepared for lots and lots of runs.

[h3] Gameplay rating: 8.5/10 [/h3]

[h1] Visuals & Sound [/h1]

[b] Visuals [/b]
The visuals in Gunfire Reborn are not mind blowing by any means, but it does have this indie charm that is so hard to hate. Everything from the characters, the NPCs, guns, even the menu is all heavily stylized. It may not be the most polished game, but it certainly has a case for being one of the most charming games. The art style is simple and easy to follow, but still gives off an incredible atmosphere. The game gives off vibes of coziness and simplicity, and just adds to the addicting nature based on the ease it gives on your eyes.

[b] Sounds [/b]
Again the sound design follows the same path its visuals take, simple and satisfying. There might not be 1:1 M16 sound bytes, but instead each gun offers a unique and pleasant pop. Each kill has an audible sound played, which makes chaining large rooms even more pleasing. The abilities have the expected mystical tones when casting, and the creeks and moans of the tomb tie it all together. The OST while not a masterpiece by any means, is adequate to the overall tone of the game. There isn’t much variety in the different songs, so be prepared to listen to the same song on repeat. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2221904310
[h3] Visuals & Sounds rating: 8/10 [/h3]

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
Gunfire Reborn is not just another roguelite doomed for early access eternity. It is a refreshing take on the genre that offers enough unique differences to be worth a look. With a focus on combat and build variety with a nice progression system, Gunfire Reborn is looking to occupy a lot of your future free time. With a price tag of $11.99 Gunfire Reborn is a hard deal to pass for anyone a fan of the genre.

[h3] Overall Score 8/10 [/h3]
